title: Snap Chip for Cross-reactivity-free and Spotter-free Multiplexed Sandwich Immunoassays
protocol: Spot cAb solutions containing 400 µg/mL antibodies and 20% glycerol in PBS onto a nitrocellulose (or functionalized glass) assay slide using an inkjet microarray spotter at a relative humidity of 60%, with 1.2 nL per spot.
Incubate the spotted assay slide at room temperature for 1 hour with a relative humidity of 60%.
Clamp a slide module gasket with 16 compartments onto the assay slide to divide it into 16 wells.
Rinse each well three times by adding 80 µL of PBS containing 0.1% Tween-20 (PBST) and shaking at 450 rpm for 5 minutes each time.
Add 80 µL of blocking solution to each well and shake for 1 hour at 450 rpm.
Remove the gasket and dry the assay slide with a stream of nitrogen.
Fix a transfer slide on the spotter deck, aligning it by pushing its bottom left corner against the bottom left corner of the deck.
Spot an array of alignment marks (solution of polystyrene micro-beads) with the same layout as for the cAbs.
Let the alignment marks dry.
Flip the transfer slide and put it back onto the spotter deck, fixing against the bottom left corner.
Prepare dAb spotting solutions containing 20 µg/mL antibodies, 20% glycerol, and 1% BSA.
Take a picture of an alignment mark using the spotter's camera.
Implement this picture into the spotting program as a fiducial.
Get the image recognition system to identify the most top left mark.
Use its coordinate as the first spot of the dAb array.
Spot 8 nL per droplet with a center-to-center spacing of 800 µm.
Place a transfer slide 1 on the inkjet spotter deck against the bottom left corner.

Spot cAbs solutions containing 400 µg/mL antibodies, 20% glycerol, and 1% BSA in PBS onto the slide with an inkjet microarray spotter at a relative humidity of 60% (0.4 nL for each spot and ~ 200 µm in diameter).
Snap the transfer slide with a nitrocellulose coated or functionalized glass assay slide using a snap apparatus.
Turn all six buttons on the side of the snap apparatus by 90 degrees to pull and lock all the plungers in the open position.
Insert the transfer slide into the slide holder in its receptacle with the clipped corner facing the fixed pogo pin.
Turn the first set of three buttons to release the plungers with the golden pogo pin.
Make sure the slides are pushed against the alignment pins.
Insert a nitrocellulose-coated slide into the snap apparatus upside-down using the pogo pins.
Release plungers with the silver pin by turning the second set of three buttons.
Push the slides against the alignment pins and close the snap apparatus by placing the top shell on the holder.
Insert the closed snap apparatus into its cage and push the closure tab down completely to bring microarrays face-to-face.
Incubate the apparatus for 1 minute under pressure, then separate the slides.
Incubate the assay slide at room temperature with a relative humidity of 60% for 1 hour.
Wash the assay slide as described in steps 1.1.3 - 1.1.5.
Block and dry the assay slide as described in steps 1.1.3 - 1.1.5.
Place another transfer slide on the inkjet spotter deck and push against the bottom left corner.
Spot dAb solutions containing antibodies at concentrations of 50 or 100 µg/mL, 20% glycerol, and 1% BSA in PBS.
Ensure each spot is 0.8 nL with a center-to-center spacing of 400 µm between spots.
Store the assay and transfer slides.
Seal both slides in an airtight bag containing desiccant.
Put sealed bags containing assay and transfer slides into a -20 °C freezer.
Retrieve the assay slide from the freezer, leaving it sealed for 30 minutes until at room temperature.
Prepare 7-point serial diluted sample solutions by spiking proteins in PBS containing 0.05% Tween-20.
Dilute human serum 4 times in PBST buffer.
Clamp a 16-compartment gasket on the assay slide.
Fill one column of 8 wells with protein dilution solutions and a protein-free PBST buffer solution by pipetting.
Pipette sample solutions into the other 8 wells on the same slide.
Incubate samples on a shaker at 450 rpm for either 1 h at room temperature or overnight at 4 °C.
Wash the slide three times with PBST on the shaker at 450 rpm, 5 min each time.
Remove the gasket and dry the slide under a stream of nitrogen gas.
Retrieve the transfer slide with dAbs from the freezer.
Keep the bag sealed for 30 min at room temperature.
Incubate the slide in a closed chamber containing 60% humidity stabilization beads for 20 min for rehydration.
Snap the transfer slide with the assay slide using a snap apparatus to transfer the dAb droplets.
Separate the slides.
Incubate the assay slide in a closed chamber containing 60% humidity stabilization beads for 1 h.
Clamp the assay slide with a 16-compartment gasket and rinse the slide 4 times using PBST on a shaker at 450 rpm, 5 min each time.
Pipette 80 µL of solutions containing 2.5 µg/mL streptavidin fluorophore in PBS into each well.
Incubate for 20 min on a shaker at 450 rpm.
Rinse the slide 3 times with PBST and once with distilled water on the shaker at 450 rpm.
Remove the gasket.
Dry the slide using nitrogen gas.
Scan the assay slide with a fluorescence microarray scanner using the 635-nm-laser.
Extract the net intensity of each spot using an analysis software (e.g., array-pro analyzer).
Calculate the limit of detection (LOD) of each protein using a statistics software.
Determine the protein concentrations in the samples.
